claim: Contractile actomyosin networks have been shown to power tissue morphogenesis.
source: Contractile actomyosin networks have been shown to power tissue morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a general statement about established knowledge in the field, supported by the broader scientific literature.

claim: The basic cellular machinery generating mechanical tension appears largely conserved across tissues.
source: Although the basic cellular machinery generating mechanical tension appears largely conserved, tensions propagate in unique ways within each tissue.
evidence: This is a general statement about established knowledge in the field.

claim: Tensions propagate in unique ways within each tissue.
source: Although the basic cellular machinery generating mechanical tension appears largely conserved, tensions propagate in unique ways within each tissue.
evidence: This is a general statement about established knowledge in the field.

claim: Retinal neuroblasts undergo fast oscillations during zebrafish optic cup morphogenesis.
source: We show that retinal neuroblasts undergo fast oscillations and that myosin condensation correlates with episodic contractions that progressively reduce basal feet area.
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data presented in the manuscript, including quantitative analysis of membrane oscillations.

claim: Myosin condensation correlates with episodic contractions that progressively reduce basal feet area.
source: We show that retinal neuroblasts undergo fast oscillations and that myosin condensation correlates with episodic contractions that progressively reduce basal feet area.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlative analysis of myosin dynamics and cell area changes presented in the manuscript.

claim: Interference with lamc1 function impairs basal contractility.
source: Interference with lamc1 function impairs basal contractility and optic cup folding.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from lamc1 morpholino knockdown experiments.

claim: Interference with lamc1 function impairs optic cup folding.
source: Interference with lamc1 function impairs basal contractility and optic cup folding.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from lamc1 morpholino knockdown experiments showing altered retinal morphology.

claim: Local ablations trigger the displacement of the entire tissue during a specific developmental window.
source: Mapping of tensile forces by laser cutting uncover a developmental window in which local ablations trigger the displacement of the entire tissue.
evidence: This claim is supported by laser ablation experiments and optical flow analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Optic cup morphogenesis is driven by a constriction mechanism.
source: Our work shows that optic cup morphogenesis is driven by a constriction mechanism and indicates that supra-cellular transmission of mechanical tension depends on ECM attachment.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence including cell tracking, myosin dynamics, and functional perturbations.

claim: Supra-cellular transmission of mechanical tension depends on ECM attachment.
source: Our work shows that optic cup morphogenesis is driven by a constriction mechanism and indicates that supra-cellular transmission of mechanical tension depends on ECM attachment.
evidence: This claim is supported by lamc1 knockdown experiments and laser ablation studies showing reduced tissue-level responses.

claim: Mechanical tensions need to be transmitted at a supra-cellular scale for organ morphogenesis to occur.
source: Regardless of the nature of the process (i.e. either cell migration, epithelial bending or cell intercalation), mechanical tensions need to be transmitted at a supra-cellular scale for organ morphogenesis to occur.
evidence: This is a general principle in developmental biology supported by established knowledge.

claim: Mechanical forces are generated by the contractile cytoskeleton of the constituent cells of a tissue.
source: Mechanical forces, however, are generated by the contractile cytoskeleton of the constituent cells of a tissue (Mammoto et al., 2013; Heisenberg and Bellaiche, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The main force generator during morphogenesis results from the molecular interaction between myosin II motors and the actin filaments at the cellular cortex.
source: The main force generator during morphogenesis results from the molecular interaction between myosin II motors and the actin filaments at the cellular cortex (Salbreux et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The actomyosin contractile apparatus sustains cortical tension, pulling cells into shape during development and tissue homeostasis.
source: This actomyosin contractile apparatus sustains cortical tension, pulling cells into shape during development and tissue homeostasis.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of cell and developmental biology.

claim: Contractile forces are transmitted to neighboring cells and to the extracellular matrix through cadherin and integrin receptors.
source: Contractile forces are then transmitted to neighboring cells and to the extracellular matrix (ECM) through cadherin and integrin receptors, allowing individual cell contributions to be integrated into tensions at the tissue/organ level (Papusheva and Heisenberg, 2010; Lecuit et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Pulsatile myosin flows precede periodic contraction of the cellular cortex in Drosophila epithelia during mesoderm invagination.
source: Initial reports, focused in epithelial constriction processes, revealed pulsatile myosin flows preceding the periodic contraction of the cellular cortex. This has been reported in Drosophila epithelia either at the apical cortex, during mesoderm invagination or germ-band extension (Martin et al., 2009; Gorfinkiel and Blanchard, 2011; Roh-johnson et al., 2012; Rauzi et al., 2010), or at the basal surface during egg chamber elongation (He et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Oscillatory actomyosin flows can be coupled to the stabilization of cells in a 'constricted' state after each pulse, resulting in a progressive reduction of the cellular apex.
source: Oscillatory actomyosin flows can be coupled to the stabilization of the cells in a 'constricted' state after each pulse, thus resulting in a progressive (i.e. ratcheted) reduction of the cellular apex (Martin et al., 2009; Rauzi et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The cell cortex may oscillate, contracting and relaxing, without a net reduction of the area over time.
source: Alternatively, the cell cortex may oscillate, contracting and relaxing, without a net reduction of the area over time (He et al., 2010; Solon et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Actomyosin flows may direct epithelial morphogenesis operating in a continuous non-pulsatile manner during zebrafish epiboly.
source: Furthermore, actomyosin flows may direct epithelial morphogenesis operating in a continuous non-pulsatile manner, as described during zebrafish epiboly (Behrndt et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The actomyosin network localizes in circumferential (junctional) belts in the vertebrate neural tube.
source: Notably, the actomyosin network localizes in circumferential (i.e. junctional) belts in the vertebrate neural tube (Nishimura et al., 2012), instead of medio-apically as observed in several Drosophila epithelia (Gorfinkiel and Blanchard, 2011; Martin et al., 2009) and in gastrulating cells in Xenopus (Kim and Davidson, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Actomyosin distribution has been analyzed during optic cup morphogenesis in vertebrates.
source: In the context of the current study, although actomyosin distribution has been analyzed during optic cup morphogenesis in vertebrates (Chauhan et al., 2009; Martinez-morales et al., 2009), its dynamics has not been examined in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and sets up the novelty of the current study.

claim: Actomyosin dynamics has not been examined in vivo during optic cup morphogenesis in vertebrates prior to this study.
source: In the context of the current study, although actomyosin distribution has been analyzed during optic cup morphogenesis in vertebrates (Chauhan et al., 2009; Martinez-morales et al., 2009), its dynamics has not been examined in vivo.
evidence: This claim establishes the novelty of the current study by indicating what has not been done previously.

claim: Optic vesicle bulging is driven by the rearrangement and epithelialization of individual cells in zebrafish.
source: Live imaging followed by cell tracking of retinal progenitors in zebrafish revealed that optic vesicle bulging is driven by the rearrangement and epithelialization of individual cells (Brown et al., 2010; Rembold et al., 2006; England et al., 2006; Ivanovitch et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In amniotes and cartilaginous fishes, optic vesicles develop by epithelial folding from an already hollow neural tube.
source: In contrast to teleosts, in amniotes and cartilaginous fishes optic vesicles develop by epithelial folding from an already hollow neural tube (Lowery and Sive, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Contractile filopodia connecting neural retina and lens epithelia adjust the final curvature of both epithelia in mouse embryos.
source: In mouse embryos, contractile filopodia connecting neural retina and lens epithelia have been shown to adjust the final curvature of both epithelia (Chauhan et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Optic cup development can be recapitulated in vitro in ES cells aggregates.
source: However, optic cup development can be recapitulated in vitro in ES cells aggregates suggesting that the morphogenetic program is to a large extent intrinsic.
evidence: This claim is supported by previous studies on ES cell-derived organoids.

claim: Optic cup invagination is driven by the apical constriction of neuroepithelial cells located at the rim between the presumptive retina and RPE domains.
source: Using this in vitro model, it has been hypothesized that optic cup invagination is driven by the apical constriction of the neuroepithelial cells located at the rim between the presumptive retina and RPE domains (Eiraku et al., 2011, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Epithelial flow through the rim contributes to neural retina expansion and optic cup folding in zebrafish.
source: Tracking of individual cells in zebrafish has shown that epithelial flow through this rim contributes to neural retina expansion (i.e. at the expenses of the RPE) and optic cup folding (Heermann et al., 2015; Kwan et al., 2012; Picker et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Basal constriction of neuroblasts is an active mechanism contributing to optic cup morphogenesis.
source: Finally, we previously postulated the basal constriction of the neuroblasts as an active mechanism contributing to optic cup morphogenesis (Martinez-Morales et al., 2009; Martinez-Morales and Wittbrodt, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: Polarized trafficking of integrin receptors toward the basal surface of epithelial cells plays an essential role during retinal morphogenesis in teleosts.
source: The polarized trafficking of integrin receptors toward the basal surface of the epithelial cells plays an essential role during retinal morphogenesis in teleosts.
evidence: This is a statement about established findings from previous work.

claim: The polarized trafficking of integrin receptors is controlled by the molecular antagonism between the trans-membrane protein opo and the clathrin adaptors numb and numb-like.
source: We showed that this process is controlled by the molecular antagonism between the trans-membrane protein opo and the clathrin adaptors numb and numb-like (Bogdanovic et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In opo medaka mutants, basal feet appear wider and disorganized in the retina.
source: In opo medaka mutants, basal feet appear wider and disorganized in the retina (Martinez-morales et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The constriction process has not been formally examined in vivo prior to this study.
source: Although this observation suggests a progressive reduction of the neuroblasts feet, the constriction process has not been formally examined in vivo.
evidence: This statement establishes the novelty of the current study.

claim: Retinal precursors undergo basal constriction during optic cup folding.
source: To formally show that basal constriction is taking place as the optic cup forms, we investigated the behavior of retinal precursors by live-imaging analysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data presented in the Results section.

claim: Retinal tissue shows complete epithelial organization shortly after 17 hpf.
source: Tissue recordings evidenced a complete epithelial organization shortly after 17 hpf, with mitotic rounding happening apically throughout the entire folding process.
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging observations.

claim: Mitotic rounding happens apically throughout the entire folding process.
source: Tissue recordings evidenced a complete epithelial organization shortly after 17 hpf, with mitotic rounding happening apically throughout the entire folding process.
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging observations.

claim: Cell involution was observed at the rim between the RPE and neural retina, particularly from 20 hpf on and at the posterior border of the cup.
source: In agreement with previous reports, cell involution was also observed at the rim between the RPE and neural retina, particularly from 20 hpf on and at the posterior (i.e. temporal) border of the cup (Heermann et al., 2015; Kwan et al., 2012; Picker et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data and citations to previous reports.

claim: GFP-caax signal becomes brighter at the basal side in the central retina as morphogenesis proceeds.
source: As morphogenesis proceeds, GFP-caax signal become brighter at the basal side in the central retina, suggesting an increased membrane density in this region.
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging observations.

claim: The increased GFP-caax signal at the basal side suggests an increased membrane density in this region.
source: As morphogenesis proceeds, GFP-caax signal become brighter at the basal side in the central retina, suggesting an increased membrane density in this region.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the imaging data.

claim: The length of the apical edge of the retina increased significantly between 17 and 24 hpf.
source: Moreover, whereas the length of the apical edge of the retina increased significantly, the basal length remained invariant (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The basal length of the retina remained invariant between 17 and 24 hpf.
source: Moreover, whereas the length of the apical edge of the retina increased significantly, the basal length remained invariant (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Retinal cell number increases 1.5-fold between 17 and 24 hpf.
source: This observation, in conjunction with the previously reported increase (1.5x) in retinal cells number within this developmental window (Kwan et al., 2012), suggests a progressive narrowing of the basal feet between 17 and 24 hpf.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: There is a progressive narrowing of the basal feet between 17 and 24 hpf.
source: This observation, in conjunction with the previously reported increase (1.5x) in retinal cells number within this developmental window (Kwan et al., 2012), suggests a progressive narrowing of the basal feet between 17 and 24 hpf.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combination of imaging data and previous cell counting studies.

claim: Cell elongation does not occur during retinal folding.
source: Cell elongation, a common phenomenon in many constricting epithelia (Sawyer et al., 2010), does not occur during retinal folding, as the width of the tissue remained constant (≈50 µm) through the process (Figure 1J–L).
evidence: This claim is supported by measurements of tissue width shown in Figure 1J-L.

claim: The width of the retinal tissue remained constant (≈50 µm) through the folding process.
source: Cell elongation, a common phenomenon in many constricting epithelia (Sawyer et al., 2010), does not occur during retinal folding, as the width of the tissue remained constant (≈50 µm) through the process (Figure 1J–L).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1J-L.

claim: Basal areas of retinal neuroblasts shrank significantly (40%) and progressively from 25.4 ± 1.7 to 15.3 ± 1.5 µm2 between 19 and 21 hpf.
source: During this developmental window, basal areas shrank significantly (40%) and progressively from 25.4 ± 1.7 to 15.3 ± 1.5 µm2 (n = 24).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of cell tracking data.

claim: Maximum basal constriction was observed between 19 and 20 hpf when most cells significantly reduced their area in a 30 min period.
source: Maximum basal constriction was observed between 19 and 20 hpf when most of the cells significantly reduced their area in a 30 min period (74.2% and 66.7% respectively; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The developmental window of maximum basal constriction coincides with the acute bending of the retinal epithelium.
source: Interestingly, this developmental window coincides with the acute bending of the retinal epithelium (Figure 1).
evidence: This is an observation correlating two phenomena from the imaging data.

claim: Apical areas of retinal neuroblasts remained constant between 19 and 20 hpf.
source: In contrast, apical areas remained constant between 19 and 20 hpf and even expanded (28%) at later stages, between 20 and 21 hpf (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Apical areas of retinal neuroblasts expanded (28%) between 20 and 21 hpf.
source: In contrast, apical areas remained constant between 19 and 20 hpf and even expanded (28%) at later stages, between 20 and 21 hpf (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Retinal cells display periodic contractions at apical and basal cell surfaces.
source: Live imaging analyses revealed periodic contractions occurring at apical and basal cell surfaces (Video 2, Figure 2), which may resemble the pulsatile behavior observed in constricting epithelia in both vertebrate and invertebrate tissues (Martin et al., 2009; Solon et al., 2009; Rauzi et al., 2010; He et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Video 2 and Figure 2.

claim: Pulsed contractions in adjacent retinal cells are mostly asynchronous.
source: As previously reported for Drosophila epithelia (Martin et al., 2009), analysis of pulsed contractions in adjacent retinal cells revealed that these are mostly asynchronous (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: 76% of apical oscillations presented no major correlation with those of their neighbors (Pearson correlation coefficient R < |0.5|).
source: The analysis of individual cells from three independent retinas showed that 76% of the apical (n = 43) and 90% of the basal (n = 46) oscillations presented no major correlation with those of their neighbors (Pearson correlation coefficient R < |0.5|).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative correlation analysis.

claim: 90% of basal oscillations presented no major correlation with those of their neighbors (Pearson correlation coefficient R < |0.5|).
source: The analysis of individual cells from three independent retinas showed that 76% of the apical (n = 43) and 90% of the basal (n = 46) oscillations presented no major correlation with those of their neighbors (Pearson correlation coefficient R < |0.5|).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative correlation analysis.

claim: Both apical and basal surfaces oscillate with a similar frequency of 50 ± 12.5 mHz (≈20 ± 5 s).
source: Comparison of the pulsatile behavior at both epithelial planes revealed significant differences. Although both surfaces oscillate with a similar frequency of 50 ± 12.5 mHz (≈20 ± 5 s; n = 26 cells), the peak-to-peak amplitude is considerably larger at the basal 11.1 ± 1.3 µm2/min than at the apical surface 4.1 ± 0.57 µm2/min (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of oscillation frequency.

claim: The peak-to-peak amplitude is considerably larger at the basal surface (11.1 ± 1.3 µm2/min) than at the apical surface (4.1 ± 0.57 µm2/min).
source: Comparison of the pulsatile behavior at both epithelial planes revealed significant differences. Although both surfaces oscillate with a similar frequency of 50 ± 12.5 mHz (≈20 ± 5 s; n = 26 cells), the peak-to-peak amplitude is considerably larger at the basal 11.1 ± 1.3 µm2/min than at the apical surface 4.1 ± 0.57 µm2/min (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cells display a progressive reduction of area at the basal side over a 25-min period.
source: Of note, whereas a progressive reduction of cell area was apparent at the basal side, cells did not display a net constriction at the apical side over a 25-min period (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Cells did not display a net constriction at the apical side over a 25-min period.
source: Of note, whereas a progressive reduction of cell area was apparent at the basal side, cells did not display a net constriction at the apical side over a 25-min period (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Apical and basal surfaces oscillate largely in an independent manner.
source: Quantitative analysis of 10 individual cells revealed a poor correlation between the pulses at apical and basal ends (R < |0.5| in all cells examined), thus indicating that these surfaces oscillate largely in an independent manner (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis of transplanted cells shown in Figure 3.

claim: Mitosis results in a transient expansion of the apical domain that is recovered once mitoses are resolved.
source: Whereas quantitative analysis of distance variation showed a transient expansion of the apical domain as the cells divide, this was recovered once mitoses were resolved (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both the apical and basal net distances at the beginning and end of mitosis did not change significantly.
source: Thus, both the apical and basal net distances at the beginning and end of the process did not change significantly (T-test; n = 10).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of distance measurements.

claim: Cell mitoses did not play a major role for optic cup formation.
source: This observation is in agreement with previous data showing that cell mitoses did not play a major role for optic cup formation (Kwan et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature and is consistent with the current observations.

claim: Actin accumulates circumferentially (junctional) rather than medially in retinal neuroepithelial cells.
source: As previously reported for vertebrate neuroepithelial cells (Nishimura et al., 2012), actin accumulated circumferentially (i.e. junctional) rather than medially as observed in constricting Drosophila epithelia (He et al., 2010; Martin et al., 2009) (Figure 4A–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4A-F and citations to previous literature.

claim: Actin accumulates at the basal surface and oscillates with a frequency similar to membrane pulses.
source: In addition, we observed that actin accumulated at the basal surface and oscillated with a frequency similar to membrane pulses (Video 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Video 4.

claim: There is a positive association between actin accumulation and basal area expansion, with a cross-correlation coefficient of 0.40 ± 0.16 (median 0.35).
source: This analysis showed a positive association between actin accumulation and basal area expansion, with a cross-correlation coefficient of 0.40 ± 0.16 (median 0.35), as calculated for 26 cells from three different experiments (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by cross-correlation analysis shown in Figure 4G-H.

claim: The positive correlation between actin accumulation and basal area changes is statistically significant compared to simulated random data.
source: Coefficients of simulated random data were significantly lower than our observations in vivo, indicating that the cells display a significant positive correlation between actin accumulation and basal area changes (Figure 4I).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Cell area expansion and actin accumulation occur simultaneously or with time lags shorter than 5 s.
source: Hence, cell area expansion and actin accumulation occur simultaneously or with time lags shorter than 5 s (i.e. our sampling rate limitation).
evidence: This is an inference from the cross-correlation analysis considering the temporal resolution of the imaging.

claim: Higher cross-correlation coefficients correspond to cells with higher actin intensity rates.
source: Furthermore, when we plotted cross-correlation coefficients as a function of the actin intensity, we observed higher coefficients corresponding to cells with higher actin intensity rates (Figure 4J).
evidence: This claim is supported by the scatter plot analysis shown in Figure 4J.

claim: The molecular mechanism responsible for fast oscillations in the vertebrate retina differs in important aspects from that controlling pulsatile behavior in constricting epithelia in Drosophila.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that the molecular mechanism responsible for the fast oscillations in the vertebrate retina differs in important aspects from that controlling the pulsatile behavior in constricting epithelia in Drosophila.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of the current data with previous literature on Drosophila.

claim: In retinal neuroblasts, peripheral actin accumulation is associated with basal ends' expansion.
source: In retinal neuroblasts, peripheral actin accumulation is associated with basal ends' expansion, whereas in Drosophila cell contraction is linked to medial condensation of actin.
evidence: This is a summary statement comparing the current findings with previous literature.

claim: In Drosophila, cell contraction is linked to medial condensation of actin.
source: In retinal neuroblasts, peripheral actin accumulation is associated with basal ends' expansion, whereas in Drosophila cell contraction is linked to medial condensation of actin.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge from previous literature on Drosophila.

claim: Myosin accumulates at the apical lens and basal retina epithelia during optic cup folding.
source: At the organ level, myosin accumulations were detected both at the apical lens and basal retina epithelia (Figure 5A–H; Video 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 5A-H and Video 5.

claim: Myosin accumulation at apical lens and basal retina is in agreement with the bending of these tissues toward their apical and basal surfaces, respectively.
source: This is in agreement with the bending of these tissues toward their apical and basal surfaces, respectively.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the myosin localization with tissue bending.

claim: Basal myosin accumulates in scattered cortical foci with an average stability of 4 ± 0.5 min.
source: Basal myosin accumulates in scattered cortical foci, which have an average stability in the range of minutes, 4 ± 0.5 min (Figure 5I–Q).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of myosin foci dynamics shown in Figure 5I-Q.

claim: Treatment with blebbistatin for 1 hr increases the stability of myosin foci to 21.5 ± 2.4 min.
source: Treatment of embryos for 1 hr with blebbistatin, a specific inhibitor that blocks myosin in an actin-detached state (Kovacs et al., 2004), severely interfered with myosin dynamics in the retina, increasing significantly the stability of the foci to 21.5 ± 2.4 min (Figure 5Q, Video 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of blebbistatin-treated embryos shown in Figure 5Q.

claim: Myosin foci correlate with basal membrane indentations.
source: Live-imaging analysis along the apico-basal retinal axis showed that myosin foci correlate with basal membrane indentations (i.e. transient shortenings of the apico-basal axis), suggesting active pulling of the basal lamina (Figure 6A–F; Video 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 6A-F and Video 7.

claim: Myosin foci suggest active pulling of the basal lamina.
source: Live-imaging analysis along the apico-basal retinal axis showed that myosin foci correlate with basal membrane indentations (i.e. transient shortenings of the apico-basal axis), suggesting active pulling of the basal lamina (Figure 6A–F; Video 7).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the correlation between myosin foci and membrane indentations.

claim: A significant shortening of the apico-basal axis occurs upon myosin accumulation for most events examined, with an average shortening of 2.3 ± 1.4 (SD) µm.
source: The analysis of 25 individual foci revealed a significant shortening of the apico-basal axis upon myosin accumulation for most of the events examined, with an average shortening of 2.3 ± 1.4 (SD) µm (Figure 6I).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6I.

claim: A large proportion of cells containing myosin foci contract significantly their basal surface.
source: Correlative analysis of basal membrane dynamics and myosin accumulation in tg(actb1:myl12.1-eGFP) embryos injected with lyn-tdTomato RNA revealed that a large proportion of the cells containing myosin foci contract significantly their basal surface (Figure 6J–P; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlative analysis shown in Figure 6J-P and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The oscillatory behavior and average area of cells neighboring those with myosin foci was not affected upon myosin accumulation.
source: In contrast, the oscillatory behavior and average area of the cells neighboring those with myosin foci was not affected upon myosin accumulation (Figure 6P; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6P and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Blebbistatin treatment stabilizes cortical myosin foci.
source: As we mentioned, myosin inhibition stabilized cortical myosin foci.
evidence: This claim is supported by the previously described blebbistatin experiments.

claim: Blebbistatin treatment impairs contractility at the basal surface of the retina.
source: Blebbistatin treatment also impaired contractility at the basal surface of the retina.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations from blebbistatin-treated embryos.

claim: Basal membrane indentations associated to myosin foci appear largely attenuated upon blebbistatin treatment.
source: Thus, basal membrane indentations associated to myosin foci appeared largely attenuated (Video 7), suggesting an inefficient mechanical coupling.
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging observations shown in Video 7.

claim: Treatment with blebbistatin for one hour abolishes the pulsatile behavior and impairs basal constriction by blocking the cells in a relaxed state.
source: In addition, when basal membrane oscillations were examined in the tg(vsx2.2:GFP-caax) line, treatment for one hour with blebbistatin abolished the pulsatile behavior and impaired basal constriction by blocking the cells in a relaxed state (Figure 6—figure supplement 2, Video 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2 and Video 8.

claim: Myosin activity is required to maintain the pulsatile dynamics.
source: This result indicates that although myosin levels do not oscillate with basal area changes, its activity is required to maintain the pulsatile dynamics.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the blebbistatin experiments.

claim: Sustained treatment with blebbistatin for 3 hr significantly delays the folding of the optic cup.
source: Finally, sustained treatment with blebbistatin for 3 hr significantly delays the folding of the optic cup (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Integrin-mediated adhesion to the ECM plays a fundamental role during optic cup folding in medaka.
source: We have previously shown that integrin-mediated adhesion to the ECM plays a fundamental role during optic cup folding in medaka (Martinez-morales et al., 2009; Bogdanovic et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: Lamc1 is a core component of laminin trimer.
source: To specifically interfere with this process in zebrafish, we knocked down lamc1, a core component of laminin trimer, the mutation of which results in ocular malformations (Domogatskaya et al., 2012; Lee and Gross, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mutation of lamc1 results in ocular malformations.
source: To specifically interfere with this process in zebrafish, we knocked down lamc1, a core component of laminin trimer, the mutation of which results in ocular malformations (Domogatskaya et al., 2012; Lee and Gross, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Sly mutants and lamc1 morphants show a similar optic cup phenotype.
source: Comparative examination of sly mutants and lamc1 morphants revealed a similar optic cup phenotype (Figure 7A–C), both interfering with the folding of the epithelium, as indicated by measurement of retinal opening angles at 24 hpf (Figure 7D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative morphological analysis shown in Figure 7A-F.

claim: Basal oscillations are not reduced upon lamc1 knockdown; their average peak amplitude is significantly increased by 45%.
source: Live-imaging analysis of tg(vsx2.2:GFP-caax) morphant retinas revealed that basal oscillations are not reduced upon lamc1 knockdown; on the contrary, their average peak amplitude was significantly increased by 45% (n = 22).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of membrane oscillations in lamc1 morphants.

claim: The progressive reduction of cellular feet observed in control retinas is severely impaired in embryos injected with lamc1 morpholinos.
source: Interestingly, the progressive reduction of the cellular feet observed in control retinas (Figure 2) was severally impaired in embryos injected with lamc1 morpholinos (lamc1Mo), and basal cell areas appeared significantly larger when compared to the control situation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Laminin-dependent adhesion to the ECM is required for effective basal constriction.
source: This observation indicates that laminin-dependent adhesion to the ECM is required for effective basal constriction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lamc1 knockdown experiments.

claim: Myosin foci are still observed in lamc1 morphant retinae.
source: Live-imaging analysis of lamc1Mo and control sibling embryos revealed that myosin foci are still observed in the morphant retinae (Figure 7G–N).
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 7G-N.

claim: In lamc1 morphant tissue, myosin foci are significantly more stable than in wild-type siblings.
source: However, in the morphant tissue, foci were significantly more stable than in the wild-type siblings, and more importantly, basal membrane indentations associated to them appeared attenuated (Figure 7O,P; Video 9).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 7O-P and Video 9.

claim: Basal membrane indentations associated to myosin foci appear attenuated in lamc1 morphants.
source: However, in the morphant tissue, foci were significantly more stable than in the wild-type siblings, and more importantly, basal membrane indentations associated to them appeared attenuated (Figure 7O,P; Video 9).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 7O-P and Video 9.

claim: Deficient adhesion to the ECM results in a less efficient transmission of mechanical tensions and reduced contractility at the basal feet.
source: This result suggests that deficient adhesion to the ECM also results in a less efficient transmission of mechanical tensions and hence reduced contractility at the basal feet.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lamc1 knockdown experiments.

claim: Laser ablations within a developmental window corresponding to a 125°–140° opening of the optic cup result in a global tissue relaxation that affects bending of the entire epithelium.
source: However, laser ablations within a developmental window corresponding to a 125°–140° opening of the optic cup resulted in a global tissue relaxation that affected bending of the entire epithelium (Video 10).
evidence: This claim is supported by laser ablation experiments shown in Video 10.

claim: At the 125°-140° stage, tension release triggers a noticeable folding of the retinal tissue toward its basal surface.
source: At this specific stage, tension release triggered a noticeable folding of the retinal tissue toward its basal surface.
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from laser ablation experiments.

claim: Maximum retraction speeds are significantly higher only for retinas displaying a 125º–140º bending.
source: Statistical analysis of optical flow data confirmed that maximum retraction speeds are significantly higher only for retinas displaying a 125º–140º bending (Figure 8F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of optical flow data shown in Figure 8F-G.

claim: The balance between tensile forces and tissue resistance that maintains organ shape is particularly unstable within a narrow developmental window that coincides with the acute constriction of the basal feet at 19 hpf.
source: This observation indicates that the balance between tensile forces and tissue resistance that maintains organ shape is particularly unstable within a narrow developmental window that coincides with the acute constriction of the basal feet at 19 hpf (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the laser ablation experiments and correlation with previous observations.

claim: Apical ablation only affects the morphology of the central retina but no peripheral retraction is observed.
source: In contrast to the global reaction observed upon basal ablation, which triggers the displacement of the peripheral retina, apical ablation only affected the morphology of the central retina but no peripheral retraction was observed (Movie 11; Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by laser ablation experiments shown in Movie 11 and Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Global relaxation of the optic cup is attenuated in lamc1 knockdown retinas at the critical 125°–140° stage.
source: The analysis of retraction speeds in laser-ablated tissues at the critical 125°–140° stage showed that global relaxation of the optic cup is attenuated in lamc1 knockdown retinas (Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claim: Laminin-mediated attachment to the ECM is essential for the transmission of mechanical tensions throughout the folding tissue.
source: This data indicates that the laminin-mediated attachment to the ECM is essential for the transmission of mechanical tensions throughout the folding tissue.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the laser ablation experiments in lamc1 morphants.

claim: Basal constriction and cell involution cooperate during eye morphogenesis in zebrafish.
source: Our observations are also consistent with these reports, thus suggesting that basal constriction and cell involution cooperate during eye morphogenesis in zebrafish.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the current data with previous reports.

claim: Basal constriction and cell involution are staggered events that overlap substantially.
source: Comparative analysis of our data and previous studies (Heermann et al., 2015) indicate that, although both mechanisms overlap substantially, they are staggered events.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the current data with previous studies.

claim: Basal constriction occurs mainly during the primary folding of the retinal epithelium between 18 and 20 hpf.
source: Whereas basal constriction occurs mainly during the primary folding of the retinal epithelium between 18 and 20 hpf, cell involution through the rim is limited during this period and becomes more prominent at later stages between 20 and 24 hpf.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temporal analysis of the current data.

claim: Cell involution through the rim is limited between 18 and 20 hpf and becomes more prominent at later stages between 20 and 24 hpf.
source: Whereas basal constriction occurs mainly during the primary folding of the retinal epithelium between 18 and 20 hpf, cell involution through the rim is limited during this period and becomes more prominent at later stages between 20 and 24 hpf.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temporal analysis of the current data.

claim: Retinal neuroblasts' periodic pulsations share some features with oscillations observed in other constricting epithelia.
source: Although, in principle, the neuroblasts' periodic pulsations share some features with the oscillations observed in other constricting epithelia (Kim and Davidson, 2011; Martin et al., 2009; Roh-johnson et al., 2012; Solon et al., 2009), there are fundamental differences.
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on the current data and previous literature.

claim: In most epithelial cells, pulsations are more regular in frequency and amplitude than in retinal precursors.
source: In most epithelial cells, pulsations are more regular in frequency and amplitude than in retinal precursors, and their average oscillation frequency range between 1 and 5 min (Gorfinkiel and Blanchard, 2011).
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on the current data and previous literature.

claim: Retinal precursors display irregular fast oscillations (≈20 s).
source: This is in contrast to irregular fast oscillations (≈20 s) here described in the zebrafish retina.
evidence: This claim is supported by the quantitative analysis of oscillation frequency in the current study.

claim: In most constricting epithelia, contractile actomyosin fibers accumulate in a medioapical domain.
source: In most of the constricting epithelia so far examined, contractile actomyosin fibers accumulate in a medioapical domain.
evidence: This is a statement about established knowledge from previous literature.

claim: From the medioapical domain, centripetal tension responsible for cell contraction is generated and transmitted to surface junctions.
source: From this domain, centripetal tension responsible for cell contraction is generated and transmitted to surface junctions (Martin et al., 2009; Roh-johnson et al., 2012; He et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: F-actin turnover is required for medioapical localization of the actomyosin meshwork, its efficient attachment to cellular junctions, and the generation of centripetal tension.
source: Interestingly, F-actin turnover is required for this medioapical localization of the actomyosin meshwork, its efficient attachment to cellular junctions, and the generation of centripetal tension (Jodoin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Both actin and myosin fibers accumulate at the cellular cortex in the zebrafish retina.
source: In contrast, our data show that both actin and myosin fibers accumulate at the cellular cortex in the zebrafish retina.
evidence: This claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the current study.

claim: Cortical distribution of actomyosin fibers has been described in the folding neural tube.
source: Cortical distribution of actomyosin fibers has also been described in the folding neural tube (Nishimura et al., 2012), thus suggesting that it may be a common feature in elongated neuroepithelial cells regardless the tissue is bending toward its apical o basal surface.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature and suggests a broader pattern.

claim: Cortical actomyosin distribution may be a common feature in elongated neuroepithelial cells regardless of whether the tissue is bending toward its apical or basal surface.
source: Cortical distribution of actomyosin fibers has also been described in the folding neural tube (Nishimura et al., 2012), thus suggesting that it may be a common feature in elongated neuroepithelial cells regardless the tissue is bending toward its apical o basal surface.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on comparing the current data with previous literature.

claim: Medial and cortical actomyosin pools have different mechanical properties in epithelial cells.
source: It has been shown that medial and cortical actomyosin pools have different mechanical properties in epithelial cells (Rauzi et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Cortical myosin accumulation does not correlate in time with the fast oscillations of the membrane.
source: Here, we show that cortical myosin accumulation does not correlate in time with the fast oscillations of the membrane.
evidence: This claim is supported by the correlative analysis presented in the current study.

claim: Myosin basal activity is necessary to maintain the fast oscillatory behavior.
source: On the contrary, blebbistatin treatment severely impaired membrane pulses, suggesting that myosin basal activity is necessary to maintain the fast oscillatory behavior.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the blebbistatin experiments.

claim: Myosin accumulates at the basal cortex in discrete foci distributed in scattered cells across the epithelial field.
source: Our data also show that myosin accumulates at the basal cortex in discrete foci, which have an average stability of approximately 4 min and are distributed in scattered cells across the epithelial field.
evidence: This claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the current study.

claim: A large proportion of retinal cells accumulating basal myosin foci are contracting both along the apico-basal and basal plane axes.
source: Remarkably, a large proportion of the retinal cells accumulating basal myosin foci are contracting both along the apico-basal and basal plane axes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the correlative analysis presented in the current study.

claim: Episodic contractions at the basal surface can be inhibited by blocking myosin activity.
source: These episodic contractions at the basal surface can be inhibited either by blocking myosin activity or by interfering with the adhesive properties of the extracellular matrix.
evidence: This claim is supported by the blebbistatin experiments presented in the current study.

claim: Episodic contractions at the basal surface can be inhibited by interfering with the adhesive properties of the extracellular matrix.
source: These episodic contractions at the basal surface can be inhibited either by blocking myosin activity or by interfering with the adhesive properties of the extracellular matrix.
evidence: This claim is supported by the lamc1 knockdown experiments presented in the current study.

claim: Retinal precursors experience non-ratcheted fast membrane oscillations.
source: According to this hypothetical model, retinal precursors would experience non-ratcheted fast membrane oscillations.
evidence: This is part of a working model proposed based on the current data.

claim: The episodic accumulation of myosin at the basal surface in scattered cells mediates their progressive (ratcheted) constriction.
source: Superimposed to these fast oscillations, the episodic accumulation of myosin at the basal surface in scattered cells would mediate their progressive (i.e. ratcheted) constriction.
evidence: This is part of a working model proposed based on the current data.

claim: Individual cell contributions add up over time to cause the constriction of the entire neuroepithelium.
source: Then, individual contributions would add up over time to cause the constriction of the entire neuroepithelium.
evidence: This is part of a working model proposed based on the current data.

claim: The global balance between mechanical tensions and tissue resistance becomes transiently unstable within a limited developmental window (19–20 hpf).
source: At a tissue level, our laser ablation experiments indicate that the global balance between mechanical tensions and tissue resistance becomes transiently unstable within a limited developmental window (19–20 hpf).
evidence: This claim is supported by the laser ablation experiments presented in the current study.

claim: The critical period of tissue instability coincides with the acute bending of the optic cup epithelium and the active constriction of the neuroblasts' feet.
source: This critical period, in which local ablations at the basal surface trigger global tissue rearrangement, coincides with the acute bending of the optic cup epithelium and the active constriction of the neuroblasts' feet.
evidence: This is a correlation observed from the current data.

claim: The ECM plays a fundamental role in the transmission of mechanical tensions generated by individual cells at the tissue level.
source: This suggests that the ECM plays a fundamental role in the transmission of mechanical tensions generated by individual cells at the tissue level.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lamc1 knockdown and laser ablation experiments.

claim: Optic cup morphogenesis largely depends on integrin function.
source: In agreement with this concept, previous reports have shown that optic cup morphogenesis largely depends on integrin function (Martinez-morales et al., 2009; Bogdanovic et al., 2012; Nakano et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The myosin-dependent generation of constriction forces in individual neuroblasts plays an essential role during optic cup folding in zebrafish.
source: Our work shows that the myosin-dependent generation of constrictions forces in individual neuroblast and their transmission at a supra-cellular scale play an essential role during optic cup folding in zebrafish.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study supported by multiple lines of evidence.

claim: The transmission of constriction forces at a supra-cellular scale plays an essential role during optic cup folding in zebrafish.
source: Our work shows that the myosin-dependent generation of constrictions forces in individual neuroblast and their transmission at a supra-cellular scale play an essential role during optic cup folding in zebrafish.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study supported by multiple lines of evidence.
